parameters: The south gate, and the Wallstraße beyond it.
The south gate: the Wallstraße runs south to Wachtburg,
the Wallweg east along the Wall to the Wallfeste.
Frontposten 3: a fortress of pale stone grown into the
Wall like a knot in a rope. Soldiers on every rampart,
and all of them are watching north.
Mori Daisuke, captain. They send me two.
Two and a ghost. The Guild's generosity knows no
bounds. …Fine. I've had worse. I've had nothing.
Here's the Wall: forty miles, thirty thousand men, and
we hold three miles of it. The old north gate is ours.
It broke the night Weißenfels fell. The Crown's been

The soldiers' name. She doesn't use it. She doesn't
use much of anything. Doesn't eat with us, doesn't sleep
much. Walked out of the snow the night Weißenfels fell
and took the breach, and nobody's asked her to leave.

Sergeant Kōno has your bunks. Sleep while you can.
The breach! Through the inner gate, go!
You held the breach with her. Against that thing.
Twenty years on this wall. I've buried a lot of better
soldiers than you, Neuling. I don't intend to bury you.
The Marshal's at the Wallfeste, a day east. Out the
south gate and take the Wallweg.
Kōno. Bunks are in the west tower, half of them empty,
and the empty ones still have boots under them.
The bell. Boots on stone, shouting on the walls.
Up! Up! They're at the breach, more than usual, and
they've brought something big! Inner gate, then the
keep, now! Falin's out there alone!

Quartermaster. Wall rates, which is to say robbery,
but at least it's honest robbery.
The inner gate. Beyond it the keep, and beyond the
keep, the breach. Mori's orders: shut until the bell.
The inner gate stands open. Beyond the keep, the
breach, and the sound of fighting.
She's going with you? Die Eiserne, leaving the
breach? …Gods keep you. Gods keep us, too.
Falin? Never seen her face. Nobody has. She holds
that gap every night and walks back in at dawn
covered in ash. Doesn't say a word.
Hounds, dead men and things in armor with nobody
inside. That's what comes. The dead men used to be
Weißenfels. We burn ours, you know. That's why.
The big one has wings. We call it the Aschenschwinge.
It took four of ours this month. Arrows don't stick.
